value.title: Introduction to Fact Storage in Language Models
value.summary: The video begins by posing the question of how large language models store factual knowledge, using the example of predicting 'basketball' after 'Michael Jordan plays the sport of'. It introduces the hypothesis that facts are stored in multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), a key component of transformer architectures, and sets up the goal of understanding how this works mechanistically.

value.title: Transformer Architecture Overview
value.summary: The video reviews the core components of transformers, including tokenization, embeddings, attention mechanisms, and the flow of information through the network. It emphasizes that vectors in high-dimensional space encode rich semantic meaning, with attention enabling context integration and MLPs handling most model parameters.

value.title: Multilayer Perceptrons and Semantic Vector Spaces
value.summary: The focus shifts to MLPs as the likely location for storing factual knowledge. The video explains how high-dimensional vector spaces can encode concepts like gender, names, and sports through directional alignment, using the example of Michael Jordan and basketball to illustrate how dot products with specific directions can represent facts.

value.title: Mechanics of MLP Computation
value.summary: The video details the internal operations of an MLP block: matrix multiplication of input vectors with learned weight matrices, addition of bias terms, and application of activation functions. It explains how these operations can detect complex patterns like full names by combining dot products across multiple directions.

value.title: Encoding Facts via Linear Projections
value.summary: The video demonstrates how MLPs can encode the fact that Michael Jordan plays basketball by designing matrix rows to detect specific name combinations and applying bias terms to ensure activation only when both name components are present, resulting in a positive output that activates the basketball direction.

value.title: Sequence Processing and Hidden States
value.summary: The video transitions to how LSTM-like mechanisms process sequences, generating hidden states that serve as inputs for further computation. It shows how these states are transformed through matrix multiplications and activation functions to capture temporal dependencies.
